official.deadline_note: Applications had to be submitted via the GIRAF platform by 18 September 2026 at 12 noon (Belgian time, UTC+1); requests to create or validate a new GIRAF account closed earlier, on 4 September 2026 at 16:00. Applications submitted after the deadline are not considered.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year, first call of the 2027-2032 five-year programme 'From Knowledge to Change'
official.status_note: ARES states that the 2027-2028 scholarship call for applications is closed and that the next call opens in August 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition fees are covered only for the specialised bachelor's degrees and specialised master's degrees; continuing education courses receive indirect mission expenses instead of tuition coverage.
benefits: International travel expenses: economy class on an IATA airline, maximum one return trip per academic year
Subsistence allowance: monthly package for 12 months (+13th reduced month)

Exceptional charges related to visa applications: variable, up to EUR 200, included in the subsistence allowance; any excess reimbursed on the basis of actual costs upon submission of supporting documents
Fees from travel inter-establishment: up to EUR 250, based on actual costs which must be justified
Insurance costs: paid directly by ARES
Tuition fees (only for the specialised bachelor's degrees and specialised master's degrees)
eligibility: Be a permanent resident and work in one of the 32 eligible countries; exception: Palestinian nationals are eligible even if they do not reside in one of these countries
Hold a higher education qualification and meet the admission requirements for the course
Have held the relevant academic degree for a maximum of 20 years at the time the course begins; this limit is increased by one year per event of childbirth and/or adoption
Provide evidence of at least two years of relevant professional experience in one of the 32 eligible countries, following the award of the last higher education qualification

Complete the application form in the language in which the course is given and attest a good written and spoken knowledge of that language; a basic knowledge of French facilitates integration into daily life in Belgium
requirements: Candidates do not need to have been previously admitted to one of Belgium's French-speaking higher education institutions in order to apply
Before applying, candidates must familiarise themselves with the specific entry requirements of each course, published on the ARES website
No follow-up will be given to applications that are not completed in full and are not accompanied by the mandatory attachments
Meeting the eligibility criteria in no way guarantees selection or eligibility for the course
Applying for an ARES scholarship is free; ARES does not charge any fees at any stage of the application or selection process
documents: Certified copies of original diplomas and certified copies of original transcripts for all years
Certificate of nationality, national identity card (voter registration card not permitted) or copy of passport

Proof of occupancy for the last 5 years and proof of residence (residence certificate, resident card or resident permit; where no such document exists in the country of residence, a signed declaration on honour)
A commitment from the employer to re-employ the employee
Pre-project (for certain courses, according to course-specific admission conditions)
selection_criteria: The quality of the academic career, assessed on diplomas, lists of courses taken, results, teaching or research activities and publications; priority to those who do not already hold a diploma with equivalent skills

Professional experience: priority to people who, after their university studies, have worked in a profession related to the development issues covered by the courses; the social impact of that experience is also considered
The potential of people to be agents of change in their own society, with particular attention to demonstrated commitment to development in addition to academic qualities
Previous scholarships: people who have previously received an ARES grant in Belgium are not eligible
Membership of a partner institution: people working in an institution partnered with ARES are given priority in the event of a tie on the other criteria

Geographic diversity of each intake, gender parity in each course (cascade effect), and maximum guarantees of return and reintegration into a profession that lets the grantee use the training for development purposes (e.g. a work contract or a formal promise of employment)
coverage: Tuition fees for specialised bachelor's and master's degrees
Subsistence allowance: monthly package for 12 months plus a 13th reduced month
International travel expenses: economy class on an IATA airline, one return trip per academic year maximum
Exceptional charges related to visa applications, up to EUR 200 included in the subsistence allowance
Inter-establishment travel fees, up to EUR 250 on justified actual costs
Insurance costs, paid directly by ARES
application_method: Applications must be submitted to ARES via the GIRAF platform (www.giraf.ares-ac.be)

Have an active GIRAF account: create an account and wait for ARES validation (a few hours to a few days; new account creation is suspended two weeks before the deadline), or reuse an account activated and used in the previous two years
Access the application form via the 'Competitive Calls' tab and click the application button once; the form then appears under 'My Tasks'
Complete the form, respecting the compulsory fields marked with an asterisk, saving progressively with 'Save as draft'
Submit the application with 'Submit my application'; once submitted, the file can no longer be modified
official.application_route: Apply online through ARES's GIRAF platform (www.giraf.ares-ac.be): create or validate a GIRAF account, open 'Competitive Calls', complete the single application form with all mandatory attachments and submit it before the call closes.
official.study_mode: One academic year integrated into the host institution's study programme (September to June or September of the following year); no part-time option is published for these scholarships
official.citizenship_residency: Permanent residents who work in one of the 32 ARES partner countries: Benin, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Cuba, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Republic of Guinea (Conakry), Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Tunisia, Uganda, Vietnam, Zimbabwe. Palestinian nationals are eligible even if they do not reside in one of these countries.
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to permanent residents of the 32 ARES partner countries (with the Palestinian exception); applicants from other countries are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Development-related international training only: in the 2027-2028 call the offer comprised one specialised bachelor's degree, eight specialised master's degrees and one continuing education course, and candidates may apply for only one of them
official.research_requirement: A pre-project must be submitted for certain courses, according to their course-specific admission conditions
official.duration: Specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees: 12 months maximum, i.e. one academic year beginning in September of year X and ending in June or September of year X+1; continuing training: 6 months maximum
official.description: ARES, the federation of higher education institutions of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation, offers nationals of an ARES partner country the opportunity to pursue a specialised bachelor's degree, a specialised master's degree or a continuing education diploma in Belgium. The international training programmes are fully integrated into the study programmes of Wallonia-Brussels Federation institutions and aim to strengthen the skills and knowledge of participants so that they become agents of change in their home institutions and in society, in support of development.
official.region: Belgium, higher education institutions of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation
official.program_type: International Training scholarship: specialised master's degree (bachelier/master de specialisation) or continuing education course
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL score is published: the application must be completed in the language in which the course is taught, with attested good written and spoken command of that language (several 2027-2028 specialised master's programmes are taught in English); a basic knowledge of French is described only as facilitating daily life in Belgium

verification.notes: Checked the live 2027-2028 call page, the call announcement, the programme overview page and the official reference document PDF (financing table, eligible countries, required documents, selection criteria and schedule). No official ARES page publishes a euro figure for the monthly subsistence package, so the stipend amount is left null rather than taken from aggregator sites.

applicant_utility.summary: The 2027-2028 ARES round closed on 18 September 2026, so there is nothing to submit right now: the next call opens around early August 2027 and gives applicants roughly six weeks. The award itself is unusually complete for a one-year specialisation master's, covering tuition, a monthly subsistence package for twelve months plus a reduced thirteenth month, one round-trip economy flight, insurance paid directly by ARES, and capped visa and inter-campus travel costs. What ARES never publishes is the euro value of that monthly package, so plan your Belgian year on conservative assumptions and treat widely circulated figures such as EUR 1,150 per month as unverified. The single biggest practical hurdle is the employer's written commitment to re-employ you afterwards, which is a mandatory attachment rather than an optional reference note.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from the 32 partner countries, ideally staff of an institution already partnered with ARES, who want a one-year specialised master's in a development field and can guarantee re-employment at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and validate your GIRAF account as soon as the call opens: validation takes from a few hours to a few days and new account creation is suspended about two weeks before the deadline, so a late start can lock you out completely

Obtain certified copies of your diplomas and of transcripts for every year of study before the window opens; certification is usually the slowest step and uncertified scans sink otherwise strong files
Secure the employer's written commitment to re-employ you after the training, since selection explicitly weighs return-and-reintegration guarantees and the commitment is a mandatory attachment
Line up two referees (academic and/or professional) and confirm the admission requirements and teaching language of your chosen course on its ARES course page before applying
Check the 20-year clock on your most recent degree, remembering that each childbirth or adoption adds a year, and gather proof of residence and work in your partner country for the last five years
Apply to one course only and draft the pre-project early if that course requires one
common_rejection_risks: Having previously received an ARES scholarship for study in Belgium: this is a hard exclusion, not a tie-breaker
A most recent degree older than 20 years at the start of the course, or fewer than two years of relevant professional experience after that degree
Applying to more than one course, or submitting in a language in which you cannot attest good written and spoken command
An incomplete file: ARES states plainly that applications not completed in full and lacking the mandatory attachments receive no follow-up at all
No credible return and reintegration plan, when the final selection criterion demands maximum guarantees such as a work contract or a formal promise of employment
Losing on nationality spread, gender parity or the partner-institution tie-break when other scores are equal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: ARES covers tuition, one round-trip economy flight, insurance, up to EUR 250 of justified inter-establishment travel and up to EUR 200 of visa costs with the excess reimbursed on receipts, so you mainly fund settling-in and personal costs, anything above those caps, and living in Belgium before the first allowance lands; because the monthly package figure is not published, treat that stipend gap as an unknown rather than assuming a round number.
document_audit: Certification is the real trap: diplomas and transcripts must be certified copies of originals, not plain scans or self-declarations
A voter registration card is explicitly not accepted as proof of nationality; use a nationality certificate, national identity card or passport copy
Residence proof must be a residence certificate, resident card or permit, and where your country issues none only a signed declaration on honour is accepted
Proof of occupancy is required for the full last five years, so a single current address letter will not satisfy it
The re-employment commitment must come from your employer, not from you, and two recommendation letters are mandatory
alerts: Timing trap: the call window is only about six weeks (3 August to 18 September in the last round), and GIRAF account creation had already stopped on 4 September, two weeks before the deadline
The deadline is Belgian time (UTC+1) at noon, which is several hours earlier than it looks from Africa, Asia or Latin America
Applying is free: ARES warns that anyone charging a fee and claiming to act on its behalf should be reported to scholarships-cooperation@ares-ac.be
Results are only communicated by June 2027, and any appeal goes to the Council of State; there is no informal review
The course list changes every cycle, so verify the programmes offered in the next call rather than reusing this year's choice
Palestinian applicants are exempt from the residency requirement, but everyone else must both live and work in one of the 32 listed countries
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Everything runs through GIRAF (www.giraf.ares-ac.be): create or validate an account, open 'Competitive Calls', click the application button once, fill the form across sessions with 'Save as draft', attach the mandatory documents, then submit; after submission nothing can be changed.
